chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Ismail al-Ju'fi and Muammar ibn Yahya ibn Sam and Muhammad ibn Muslim and Zurara, who said: We heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying:
Dissimulation (Taqiyya) applies to everything the son of Adam is compelled to, so Allah has permitted it for him.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةُ: Dissimulation or concealment of faith/status to avoid harm

ai.seo_question: What is the scope of Taqiyya in Shia Islam according to the Imams?
ai.summary: This foundational hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in al-Kafi broadens the scope of Taqiyya beyond mere survival to include any situation of compulsion (idtirar), affirming its permissibility across all aspects of life. It underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that divine concession allows believers to conceal their faith or status to preserve religious integrity when faced with external pressure. This principle is central to understanding the historical resilience of the Ahl al-Bayt and their followers under varying political and social conditions.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibn Azina, from Ismail Al Ju’fy and Moammar Bin Yahya Bin Sam and Muhammad Bin Muslim and Zurara who all said: 
‘We heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying:
‘The dissimulation (Taqiyya) is with regards to everything the son of Adamas is compelled to. So Allahazwj has Permitted it for him’.
en.sarwar: 18. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ibn ‘Udhaynah from Isma’il al-Ju’fi and Mu’ammar ibn Yahya ibn Sam and Muhammad ibn Muslim and Zurara who have said the following: “We heard abu Ja’far (a.s.) saying, ‘
Al-Taqiyyah is whenever the son of Adam is compelled; Allah has made it lawful for him.’”
